issue.title: Feature request: support non-streaming requests in the group FirstToken timeout
issue.body:
## Request

Please consider applying the existing routing group's `FirstToken` timeout to **non-streaming requests (`stream:false`)** as well.

This would let a group switch to its next candidate when a non-streaming upstream stalls before producing response content, just as it can for a streaming request. It need not introduce a new setting or change the cancellation/cooldown policy.

## Concrete use case

Hindsight sends non-streaming Chat Completions requests. If a candidate stalls, the existing `FirstToken` setting does not advance to the next candidate; the caller can reach its own HTTP timeout and disconnect before the gateway gives the fallback a chance.

In the v0.1.1612-based code we investigated, the gateway sets the first-content timer only when `streams` is true:

```go
if isGroup && firstToken > 0 && !last && streams {
    hw.firstWait = time.Duration(firstToken) * time.Second
}
```

There is a second relevant detail: receiving JSON response headers marks the reply as `whole`, which the existing `holdWriter.started()` treats as started even if no body content has arrived. Extending the timer must also handle this header-only stall.

## Expected behavior

- Reuse the group's existing `FirstToken` duration for `stream:false`.
- If the upstream has supplied no response-body content within that duration, cancel that attempt and try the next candidate while the caller is still connected.
- Headers alone must not satisfy the first-content deadline.
- Preserve existing semantics: zero disables the budget, a final candidate is not interrupted by this fallback budget, and a reply already started is not cut off by it.

For a fully buffered non-streaming upstream, the gateway cannot observe the model's actual first generated token. The measurable equivalent is **first response-body content / time to response**, not internal generation TTFT. This request is about that fallback deadline, not an overall completion timeout.

## Reproduction and local check

Our regression serves two candidates: the first immediately sends JSON headers and then stalls; the second returns a valid JSON completion. With a one-second group budget and a three-second caller deadline, the original code reaches the caller deadline instead of returning the fallback. With the timeout applied to non-streaming first content, the second candidate answers after approximately one second.

The regression, repeated targeted race tests, and an isolated compiled-binary HTTP smoke test pass. Our local fork is deployed, and a non-streaming production request using Hindsight's caller credential also returned successfully; that production smoke check does not by itself establish a long-term latency improvement.

Reference implementation:
https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43

That local commit contains both this change and a separate optional cancellation-cooldown experiment, now tracked in #3791. **This issue asks only for the non-streaming timeout extension**; the two features can be reviewed and accepted independently, and any PR for this issue should isolate the timeout changes.

The full Go suite has unrelated failures reproduced on our unchanged production baseline; the local patch does not claim a green full suite.

Would this extension of `FirstToken` fit the intended routing behavior?

comments.body:
**Update — 2026-10-28: the original implementation needs a regression fix.** Follow-up [b48a91bb](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b48a91bb75d098ab3e004503e07feac9b1c6ca46) is now pushed to the same branch.

Extending `holdWriter.watch` to non-streaming requests also enabled its SSE keepalive path. A silent candidate waiting longer than 15 seconds could therefore commit **HTTP 200 + text/event-stream** before the real result arrived. Later JSON answers and HTTP errors were emitted as SSE; Hindsight's non-streaming OpenAI client received a string rather than a completion object and reported missing choices. This is a wire-format regression, not evidence that the model returned an empty choices array.

The fix requires `h.streams` in `keepQuiet`. It preserves non-streaming first-response timeout/fallback and the separate cooldown policy. The earlier one-second header-only test missed the silent, longer-than-keepalive case and did not assert the response format.

New tests cover silent/header-only fallback and delayed 200/503 JSON for Chat, Responses and Messages. Reverting only the production fix makes them fail with early SSE, including 503 becoming 200. Targeted checks pass 20 race repetitions on the fix branch and on our isolated v0.1.1767 integration. The compiled integration binary returns JSON after a 20.011-second wait and an 18.012-second fallback over real HTTP.

Native/Linux/Windows vet and builds pass; the full integration gateway suite passes. The whole repository suite is **not green**: existing #3924, #3854, #3919, container-sensitive checks, and a separately repaired #3487 quota fixture are documented in [PATCHES.md](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/b48a91bb75d098ab3e004503e07feac9b1c6ca46/PATCHES.md#non-streaming-sse-regression-follow-up-2026-10-28).

This follow-up is ready for our deployment integrator to cherry-pick; I have **not deployed it**. The timeout feature remains independently separable from #3791.

**v0.1.1767 integration handoff:** [`fix/hindsight-nonstream-sse-1767`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/hindsight-nonstream-sse-1767) contains [b6f71ebd](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b6f71ebd8e7824148fc658347ba0561505deb15e) (quota test fixture) followed by [dfd128ca](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/dfd128ca39ecca7a6e792141fea33b2ce77ad8ed) (the same SSE fix, with the `PATCHES.md` history conflict resolved). Both are based on our `c70e0610` v0.1.1767 integration. Cherry-pick those two commits in that order onto the corresponding deployment line; do not also cherry-pick b48a91bb. This is a prepared source handoff, not a deployment.

---

**Original implementation/deployment record (before this correction):**

The implementation is already saved in our fork on [`fix/hindsight-nonstream-cooldown`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/hindsight-nonstream-cooldown), in commit [dd670e6](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43), and was deployed to our own production instance.

For **this issue's non-streaming timeout extension**, the relevant implementation is:

- [Apply the existing group FirstToken timer to non-streaming requests](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43/internal/gateway/gateway.go#L2560).
- [Do not treat JSON headers alone as first response content](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43/internal/gateway/fallback.go#L2653).
- [TestNonstreamFirstResponseFallsBack](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43/internal/gateway/nonstream_cooldown_test.go#L18): a header-only stall must yield to a candidate that returns JSON before the caller's deadline.

The regression fails with the original gateway logic. Targeted repeated race tests and a compiled-binary HTTP smoke test passed; the latter observed fallback at approximately one second with a one-second budget. The full suite has unrelated failures also reproduced on the unchanged production baseline, so this is not a claim of a green full suite.

**The linked commit also contains the separate optional cancellation-cooldown experiment in #3791.** That policy is not required for this feature; a future PR for #3788 should isolate the timeout changes above. Sharing the implementation here for review, without coupling acceptance of the two proposals.

The observability proposal previously described in this comment is now tracked independently in **#3948 — distinguish protocol errors and client-reported failures from HTTP success**.

That feature request contains the scope, acceptance criteria, implementation ([56eb1ba1](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/56eb1ba11c1b59b0002558c37ad74e2069250220)) and validation limits. It covers protocol-error visibility, explanations for missing speed, and error provenance; it can be reviewed separately from this issue's non-streaming FirstToken timeout extension and #3791's cooldown policy.

The earlier SSE transport regression explanation and fix remain in [the preceding implementation comment](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3788#issuecomment-6432514407). This issue remains focused on the timeout feature and its transport correctness.

issue.title: Feature request: opt-in model cooldown and capped exponential backoff for client cancellations (499)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Request

Would an **opt-in model-level cooldown for client cancellations (499)**, with exponential backoff and a configurable rest cap, be useful for deployments using busy free models?

This is a routing-policy proposal for maintainer feedback. It can be evaluated independently of #3788, which only asks for non-streaming support in the existing group `FirstToken` timeout.

## Concrete use case

Hindsight sends background, non-streaming Chat Completions requests and cancels them when its client deadline expires. On our v0.1.1612-based gateway, a 24-hour Hindsight sample had 3,941 gateway requests, including 603 client cancellations. One free model accounted for 567 cancellations, with median cancellation time about 119.9 seconds.

These 499s are logged by Magpie when the client disconnects; they are not 499 responses from the model vendor. The existing cancellation path does not rest the model, so subsequent requests can keep paying the same timeout when it remains overloaded. Our operator would prefer a deliberately aggressive cooldown for selected free models during these periods.

## Optional behavior to consider

- Opt selected models into cancellation-driven cooling. Scope the state to **provider + account/key + exact model**, so another model on the same provider remains usable.
- Count cancellation only after an upstream attempt starts. Cancellation while queued, or during a retry pause, should not penalize the model.
- Back off exponentially, for example **1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60, 60… minutes**, with a configurable model-level cap. **60 minutes is our deployment's preference**, not a proposed mandatory global default. A successful response resets the ladder; the cooldown plus the next request's latency must not accidentally trigger the quiet-period reset.
- Honor the cooldown even if every candidate is resting. Otherwise a last-candidate probe on each new request defeats the policy. When nothing else is available, return 503 with `Retry-After`; held requests should neither increment nor extend the rest.

The opt-in is important: the gateway cannot reliably distinguish a client's timeout from a user deliberately pressing Stop. Counting all cancellations by default would therefore be inappropriate for many interactive users. An opted-in operator accepts that manual in-flight cancellation can cool that model too.

## Configuration and local experiment

The desired capability is a model-specific cooldown/backoff policy and a `restCap`-like upper bound. Existing `restCap` is provider-wide. Our fork uses provider JSON `"modelCooldown":{"<exact-model-id>":60}` to combine the opt-in and cap without changing other models' settings; this spelling is only a local experiment, not a prescribed upstream API. `RestCapOff` still overrides failure resting.

Our local implementation shares the existing slow-start ladder for slow first responses and opted-in cancellations. It has no GUI editor and keeps the existing process-local failure counter. We have deployed it locally, but have not yet established a multi-hour production improvement.

Reference implementation (also contains the separate non-streaming timeout change):
https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43

Targeted regressions cover model/account isolation, reaching and staying at the cap even after a two-minute subsequent timeout, success resetting the count, and zero upstream probes during cooldown. Repeated race tests and a compiled-binary HTTP smoke test pass. The full suite is not green on our unchanged production baseline either; the patch does not claim to fix those unrelated failures.

Related: #2945 (all-resting candidates still being called), #2008 (rest ladder caps/state).

Do maintainers see this cancellation pattern in real deployments, and would an optional model-level policy be appropriate? If so, should it extend the existing rest configuration or use a separate opt-in?

issue.title: Quota card: an unknown usage amount renders as a full allowance; a plugin span sent in ms is read as seconds, charting a window start at 2024-01-29

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Observed (live, 2026-10-24, provider `cloudflare-workers-ai` from `@magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth` 0.0.3)

- The Workers AI account had consumed **10,756.27 of its 10,000/day free Neurons** (per Cloudflare's own GraphQL Analytics, `aiInferenceAdaptiveGroups.sum.totalNeurons`); every inference returned `429 / code 3036: you have used up your daily free allocation of 10000 neurons`.
- The provider's quota card nevertheless showed **`10,000 / 10,000 Neurons · 剩余 100%`**, freshly refreshed.
- `quota-history.json` on disk recorded: `\{"left": 100, "start": "2024-01-29T00:00:00Z", "resetsAt": "2026-10-25T00:00:00Z"\}` — the chart's x-axis rendered that start as 「1月29日 10:00」.
- The gateway had actually put the provider on rest for the rest of the day, so the card said the exact opposite of reality at the moment it mattered.

## Root cause A — an unknown amount is rendered as an untouched allowance

1. `internal/plugin/providers.go:1079`: `Amount float64 `json:"amount"`` — a plugin returning JSON `"amount": null` ("I don't know what was used") decodes silently to `0`. "Unknown" is unrepresentable in the type.
2. `internal/gui/assets/app.js:13937`: `const amount = Math.max(0, w.amount || 0), n = quotaLeft ? Math.max(0, w.limit - amount) : amount;` — `null || 0` again, so remaining = limit − 0 = 100% and the progress bar draws full.

Suggestion: `Amount *float64`, and when it is nil render 「已用 —」 with no filled bar (or show the window's `display` text) instead of a full allowance. Any plugin that reports a window without an amount currently misleads the same way.

## Root cause B — span unit mismatch (plugin fixed, but the card chart is where it shows)

The plugin sent `span: 86400000` (ms). `UsageWindow.span` is documented as **seconds** (`internal/plugin/providers.go:1082`), so `internal/provider/quota_history.go:189-192` (`Start = ResetsAt − span`) backed off **1,000 days**: 2026-10-25T00:00Z − 86,400,000 s = 2024-01-29T00:00Z — precisely the bogus axis start.

Plugin-side fix is in magpie-community/plugins#366 (sends `86400` now). Core-side, a defensive clamp would keep any future misbehaving plugin from charting a two-year window: e.g. treat `span` beyond `ResetsAt − now` (or > ~400 days) as invalid and fall back to the name-derived span.

## Environment

magpie `0.1.1364` (official image, Linux/docker).

issue.title: Feature request: distinguish protocol errors and client-reported failures from HTTP success in request observability

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem

A request can show HTTP 200 and no token/s in Usage even when the response is unusable by the client. A normal short non-streaming response can look the same. This makes prolonged failures difficult to notice.

Our motivating case was the non-streaming SSE regression discussed in #3788: a keepalive committed HTTP 200 and SSE before the real JSON response arrived. Hindsight's non-streaming client then reported missing choices. That exception did **not** prove the model returned an empty choices array; the client received the wrong response format.

The transport regression and its fix belong in #3788. This feature request separately tracks the observability improvement and can be reviewed independently of the timeout extension and #3791's cooldown policy.

## Requested behavior

1. **Keep HTTP status and observed errors separate.** If Magpie can identify a request/response protocol mismatch, record a protocol error while retaining the actual HTTP status, including 200. Usage should clearly show `200 · Protocol error`, with an explanation in the details.
2. **Explain missing speed.** Normal requests without a usable timing sample should show non-streaming/untimed or insufficient sample, with a specific reason. Absence of token/s must not imply success or failure.
3. **Identify error provenance.** Existing client-reported errors or client-log errors should retain their original text and clearly identify their source. For example, `ProviderResponseError: missing choices` supplied by a client is a client report, not an independently verified gateway diagnosis.
4. **State the visibility boundary.** HTTP 200 does not establish that Hindsight or another client parsed, accepted or used the response successfully.

## Acceptance criteria and scope

- A known non-streaming response-format mismatch, malformed JSON envelope, missing response array or empty Chat `choices` is visibly failed despite HTTP 200.
- Routing, Usage, Recent calls and request observers retain the gateway-observed error.
- Valid tool calls, refusals and empty text are not rejected. Error-looking words such as `ERROR` or `Traceback` inside normal model output do not trigger failures.
- Client-reported errors remain visibly sourced even when the report has no HTTP status.
- The diagnostic check does not change the response already sent, retry the request or impose cooldown.
- No Hindsight log collector, new feedback endpoint, report-to-request merging or historical reclassification is proposed in this patch.
- The initial implementation checks known non-streaming Chat, Responses and Anthropic envelopes using the existing bounded capture. It does not parse truncated/encoded captures or validate streaming response bodies.

## Implementation available for review

- Fork branch: [fix/request-protocol-visibility](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/request-protocol-visibility)
- Implementation: [56eb1ba1](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/56eb1ba11c1b59b0002558c37ad74e2069250220)
- [Scope, validation and integration notes](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/56eb1ba11c1b59b0002558c37ad74e2069250220/PATCHES.md#request-protocol-and-client-error-visibility-2026-10-28)

The implementation is based on our v0.1.1767-p2 integration source, `1207467e`. It has not been deployed by this work.

Old-code regression failures were confirmed. Protocol/capture/routing/OTLP checks pass 20 race repetitions; affected UI tests pass Chromium and WebKit, with all five languages covered for the new UI; native/Linux/Windows vet and builds pass. A final gateway run passes in 318.139s with five reproduced baseline failures excluded. **The complete repository suite is not green**; exact exclusions and other reproduced baseline failures are documented in the linked notes.
